description_en: Two stone memorial pillars from approx. 14th century.The two pillars are located in Kumā, a locality 300 meters south-east of Cilkhāyā. In Cilkhāyā are standing twośikharatemples (DLK0250) that can be roughly dated from between the 14th and 16th century (Sharma 1972).Both pillars are carved on the southern sides. Despite the poor quality of the stone it is possible to distinguish, on both pillars, a horserider. Pillar 001 contains an additional anthropomorphe, visibly on foot. This may describe two warriors, or a warrior and a relative. The broken arc shape of the pillars and their iconography is most often encountered in the districts of Jumla and Kalikot. In the absence of dated inscription it is merely possible to situate these artefacts around the 14th-15th century.Stone pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th century. They are installed to honor the memory of deceased persons, mostly warriors, as is illustrated in Kumā (Andolfatto 2019).
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, D. C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université. Sharma, P. R. 1972. Preliminary Study of the Art and Architecture of the Karnali Basin, West Nepal. Paris: CNRS.
